item.title: SALES: The 10 best places to visit in December 2026
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
The 10 best places to visit in December 2026 The ideal December getaway is different for every traveler. For some, strolling through Europe's sparkling holiday markets is the dream, while for others, chasing the thrill of fresh powder makes the month great. Or, if you prefer to kick back, the warm waters of Mexico's Riviera Maya are just the ticket. Plus, major hotel openings, new flight routes and seasonal celebrations make December an especially exciting time to travel. Whether you're chasing sunshine in the Southern Hemisphere, looking for far-flung adventures or want to snuggle up in a winter wonderland, these are the 10 best places to visit in December. Japan's legendary powder snow and frosted alpine scenery is going to be easier to reach this winter. Starting Dec. 11, United Airlines is launching three weekly seasonal nonstop flights between San Francisco International Airport (SFO) and Sapporo's New Chitose Airport (CTS), marking the first nonstop service between the continental U.S. and Hokkaido. From Sapporo, travelers can head to Niseko, one of Japan's premier ski destinations, where a new eight-passenger gondola is set to debut for the 2026-27 ski season. December is an especially enticing time to visit, when a winter glow settles over Niseko and the region's famous snow season gets underway. Extra bonus: You can take a break from skiing and snowboarding to warm up in traditional Japanese hot spring surrounded by the snowy mountain scenery and the area's restaurants offer a chance to sample Hokkaido specialties, including warm bowls of rich ramen. TPG tip: There's even more news in Niseko: Moxy Niseko Village, one of our most anticipated points hotels in 2026, just opened, bringing the brand's playful style, and reasonable prices, to a mountain retreat with direct ski-in, ski-out access. After a day on the slopes, unwind in the efficient and tech savvy rooms, grab drinks at Bar Moxy or explore the area's restaurants and shops. Rates in December start at $134 per night or 64,000 Marriott Bonvoy points, however there is limited availability during high season for the latter. If your head is filled with visions of mulled wine, spiced cookies, twinkling lights and sweet treats, then put Budapest on your December travel list. The Hungarian capital sparkles in December with two particularly large holiday markets, one at Vorosmarty Square and the other at St. Stephen's Basilica. At Vorosmarty, purchase local handmade crafts and Hungarian items, including soaps and spices. Meanwhile, at the St. Stephen's market, you'll find copious food options to sample with your forralt bar (mulled wine), including large fried flatbread called lagos that come heaped with toppings both savory (if in doubt, go for the sour cream covered with grated cheese) or sweet (Nutella is a popular choice). Enjoy it while you watch the light show projected on the basilica. Two more festive ways to spend time in Budapest in December: take a nighttime cruise along the Danube River to see the House of Parliament and the Royal Castle cast in a golden glow or visit the Hungarian State Opera, a restored Baroque gem, to see The Nutcracker. TPG tip: Keep the festive spirit going at the New York Cafe, often called "the most beautiful cafe in the world." It's a candy box of crystal, marble and opulent golden details. Sip a hot chocolate or a cocktail, order a gorgeous layer cake or warm up with a bowl of goulash. There's usually a long line to get in, but if you stay at the elegant Anantara New York Palace Budapest Hotel, special tables are reserved for hotel guests, sans wait. Opt for the elaborate breakfast, for hotel guests only, and you'll be able to nibble Hungarian crepes under the grand chandeliers, and without the crowds, too. Rooms from $407 a night in December and can be booked through Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts. The Hilton Budapest Hotel is about as close as possible to sleeping in Buda Castle itself. The hotel is a former 13th-century church on Castle Hill just steps from St. Matthias Church and Fisherman's Bastion. December rates start from $175 or 54,000 Hilton Honors points per night. Looking for an easy-to-reach warm-weather escape in December? The Riviera Maya presents an ideal option. With daytime temperatures averaging 81 degrees Fahrenheit and balmy evenings around 73 degrees, it's an ideal time for beach lounging, snorkeling, exploring ancient Mayan ruins or jumping into a cenote (natural swimming hole) without the intense heat or humidity of summer. December also marks the start of the dry season, meaning clearer skies and no chance of fall's extended hurricane season. Even better, holiday festivities are in full swing — including the vibrant Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on Dec. 12, and Christmas and New Year's celebrations at many resorts, complete with beachfront dinners, live entertainment and cultural performances. Be sure to stop at local markets offering traditional holiday foods such as sweet fried bunuelos and tamales (even though you may have seen them year-round, they're a Christmas tradition). TPG tip: December is the perfect time to try out the debut of Kimpton's first all-inclusive resort, the beachfront Kimpton Tres Rios. Set in a 340-acre nature preserve, the property has multiple pools, including separate ones for kids and adults, a 10,000 square foot spa and seven restaurants and bars. Guests can also take advantage of the resort's Tres Rios natural setting with kayaking, snorkeling or exploring the fresh-water cenotes. Rates start at $427 per night based on double occupancy, or 35,000 IHG One Rewards points per night. There are few things as memorable as visiting the Big Apple when it's covered with sparkling holiday frosting and the entire city feels like a Hallmark movie set. Your holiday must-see list will be never-ending, but some classic must-dos include a stop by Fifth Avenue for some last-minute shopping, an icy spin on the Wollman Rink after a festive stroll through Central Park, a visit to Macy's Santaland if you have kids in tow, a performance of "Christmas Spectacular Starring The Radio City Rockettes" and a visit to Brooklyn neighborhood Dyker Heights for some of the most truly jaw-dropping festive holiday lights anywhere in the country. Plus, Rockefeller Center is celebrating 90 years of The Rink with an extra dose of holiday magic this season, transforming both sides of the iconic ice skating rink into festive tree-viewing destinations, including cozy Holiday Chalets where you can sip and dine. This year's tree lighting celebration takes place Dec. 2 in 2026. Bank of America Winter Village at Bryant Park has the largest holiday market in the city, plus dining, intimate igloos, skating AND the chance to meet Santa on select dates. The tree lighting here also takes place Dec. 2. (Heads up, this is going to be a really busy night in the city, so plan accordingly.) Want to give back while you're in NYC? NH Collection New York Madison Avenue's "Hotels with a Heart" program combines festive decorations, seasonal cocktails and live jazz with a fundraiser that donates 100% of sales from the hotels's handblown glass heart ornaments to St. Jude Children's Research Hospital (rooms from $686 a night in December). TPG tip: We're anxiously awaiting the opening of Hotel Plaza Athénée Nobu New York this month (although at press time the opening date was still set as as "late 2026"). When it does open, the nearly century-old building with a famed history of hospitality will have 145 rooms, suites with indoor-outdoor glassed terraces, a Japanese onsen, a spa and a wellness center and, of course, an outpost of the iconic namesake sushi restaurant. Rates still to be announced. Egypt becomes pleasantly mild in December, making it an ideal time to explore the country's ancient wonders, including those in Cairo and along the Nile River. Don't miss the Grand Egyptian Museum, located near the Giza pyramids, which opened last November and continues to draw crowds. Filled with wonders such as the obelisk of King Rameses II and the golden burial mask of Tutankhamun, this will continue to be a hot ticket for a long time to come. Reservations are required in advance, and walk-ups are not permitted; use this website to secure your tickets (there are many imposter sites, unfortunately). Nile River cruising is also having a moment, with several newly launched ships, including Abercrombie & Kent's Nile Seray, an A&K Sanctuary, which has 32 suites and sails between Luxor and Aswan on four-night journeys that combine exclusive archaeological access with exceptional dining programs. Viking also expanded its Egyptian fleet, now numbering a dozen ships, with the recent additions of Viking Sekhmet and Viking Ptah that, like other ships on the Nile, visit the enormous temples of Karnak and the Valley of the Kings, as well as many other iconic sites of the ancient world. TPG tip: For a luxe stay in Cairo, head to the pampering oasis of the St. Regis Cairo. The 36-story property has 366 guest rooms, suites and apartments, as well as seven bars and restaurants on-site. Rates start at $500 or 53,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night in December. Lyon may be known as the capital of gastronomy in France — it was the home of famed French chef Paul Bocuse. But in December, food comes second to the glowing Festival of Lights. The annual event, Dec. 5-8, 2026, started when residents lit candles to thank the Virgin Mary. It is now a four-day spectacle of light shows, art installations and performances across the city. The festival centers around Saint-Jean Cathedral, which transforms into a multi-hued Gothic wonder through sophisticated light projections. And of course, cuisine is still an integral part of a visit to Lyon (the city is at the center of Vallee de la Gastronomie). Stroll through the Paul Bocuse Food Hall to shop for glistening pyramids of candied fruits and towers of hand-poured chocolates — both popular seasonal options. Then pull up a stool at an oyster bar for fresh-shucked oysters and a glass of sparkling wine. For an even more festive meal, try Les Loges in the reopened Cour des Loges Lyon, a Radisson Collection Hotel (rooms from $297 per night). The charming chef, Anthony Bonnet, secured a coveted Michelin star for the restaurant. The centuries-old space is a grand setting for a multicourse menu that makes the most of seasonal ingredients like locally foraged mushrooms, hazelnuts and a hay-infused beef bouillon. TPG tip: Villa Maia, perched atop Fourviere Hill, offers views of the entire old town below. Stays include access to the property's Roman baths, a deep-soaking relaxation pool, a sauna and a steam room. Prices in December start at $308 per night. If you hold the right Amex card, you can book it through Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts to get perks like complimentary daily breakfast for two and guaranteed 4 p.m. late checkout. The restored Intercontinental Lyon — Hotel Dieu by IHG occupies a palatial 18th-century building on the Rhone River within walking distance of the old town. Rooms start at $247 or 62,000 IHG One Rewards points per night in December. December is one of the best times to experience Argentine Patagonia, when the Southern Hemisphere summer brings long daylight hours and ideal conditions for exploring its vast wilderness. Adding a new reason to visit, Explora El Calafate is set to open Dec. 4, 2026, introducing a luxury lodge in the Patagonian steppe with sweeping views toward Lake Argentino, the Andes and the distant Perito Moreno Glacier. The glacier is the region's star attraction. Located within Los Glaciares National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Perito Moreno is a spectacular expanse of ice that you can admire from panoramic walkways, approach by boat or experience on guided ice-trekking excursions. Beyond the glacier, there's hiking across the plains, horseback riding through remote valleys and spending time with the turquoise lakes and jagged peaks that this rugged corner of South America is known for. TPG tip: Explora El Calafate is located in the Chorrillo Malo estancia. The long, low 10-room lodge looks like a train snaking through the vast steppes as it blends into the surrounding scenery. It's a key new link in Explora's Patagonia Network, combinable with the new Explora Torres del Paine in Chile and Explora Patagonia National Park and Explora El Chaltén in Argentina for a multi-lodge, cross-border itinerary. Rooms in December start at $1,402 per night, all inclusive, and include all meals and beverages, activities and airport transfers. If you're an arts and culture lover, you're going to want to add Memphis to your travel plans this December. The Memphis Art Museum opens Dec. 6 in a stunning Herzog & de Meuron-designed building right on the Mississippi riverfront. The $222 million campus is a landmark moment for Memphis and one of the most significant museum openings in the South in decades. The inaugural exhibition, Making Beauty: Hooks Brothers Studio, 1907–1984, honors a historic African American photography studio that documented local Black communities in the urban South. The exhibit is co-presented with the nearby National Civil Rights Museum, which reopened this past September and is worth a special visit as well. While you're in Memphis, you'll want to hit Beale Street not just for all the live music fun, but also for the Memphis Holiday Parade and Market on Dec. 12, which brings marching bands, festive floats and dozens of local vendors to Handy Park. Add to the holiday spirit with MOSH's (Memphis Museum of Science and History) Enchanted Forest Festival of Trees with a snow-covered village, miniature trains and holiday laser shows in the planetarium. TPG tip: The Hyatt Centric it is perfectly situated for all things Memphis with a prime location on historic Beale Street and Beck & Call rooftop lounge is a perfect perch to check out the neighborhood's holiday lights. Rates in December from $171 or 12,000 points per night. Singita, which boasts some of Africa's most luxurious safari lodges, is expanding into Botswana's biodiversity-rich Okavango Delta with one of our most anticipated hotel openings for 2026. The hotly anticipated Singita Elela launches on Dec. 11, giving guests the opportunity to experience the stunning wetland region in all seasons through a conservation-focused lens and in complete luxury. Guests of Elela will have exclusive access to more than 420,000 acres of untouched wilderness with the chance to get up close and personal with the thousands of species that call it home via safari drives, dugout mokoro boats or walking safari options. TPG tip: Unlike most traditional safari lodges where there are private accommodations and shared public spaces at a single camp, Elela comprises 10 stilted, entirely private camps, with five one-bedroom and two two-bedroom options and and one four-bedroom camp that sleeps eight. Each camp includes a dedicated vehicle, guide, tracker, camp manager and even a private arrival point. The four-bedroom camp amps that up to include two private vehicles plus a wine cellar, a workout room and a personal chef. Rates for the one bedroom camps start at $3,100 per adult and $1,550 per child and the four-bedroom camp starts at $22,830 per night, per group. (Note that children of all ages are allowed in camp, but there are age restrictions for activities.) For travelers looking to trade snowflakes for sunshine, New Zealand's South Island offers a summer escape in December, with long, sunny days ideal for exploring dramatic landscapes, coastal towns and renowned wine regions. United Airlines resumes its seasonal nonstop service between San Francisco International Airport (SFO) and Christchurch Airport (CHC) on Dec. 2, 2026, making it easy to reach the Southern Hemisphere destination. The route, United's southernmost, makes Christchurch a convenient starting point for a South Island adventure. In Christchurch, explore the city's gardens, riverside dining scene and nearby beaches, or venture into the surrounding countryside for outdoor adventures. Wine lovers can head to the Waipara Valley, a popular wine region known for its Riesling and Pinot Noir. Tpg tip: Base yourself in Queenstown for a standout new hotel option on South Island. Avani Queenstown, which debuted in September 2026, offers a contemporary luxury retreat nestled on the shores of Lake Wakatipu and a mix of traditional hotel rooms and one- and two-bedroom apartments. Rates from $277 per night in December. Related reading: Terms & restrictions apply. See rates & fees.

item.title: SALES: We Tested Them All: 100 Cost-Conscious Gift Ideas You'll Love to Give
item.description:
Source: PCMag
Is your son's phone battery slowly dying? Have your friend's earbuds gone AWOL? If you're like most people with a holiday shopping list a mile long, you need thoughtful yet affordable options for the tech lovers in your life. But finding cheap, high-quality gear isn't easy, especially given volatile global markets and outrageous supply costs. Don't worry! We've done extensive analysis and research to find the tech that delivers both performance and value. Our experts have tested everything on this list, from beefy desktop PCs to slim smartphones, couch-potato TV gear to advanced health gadgets, engaging PC games to serious security apps. We update this story monthly, so the values are always fresh. Go ahead and dig into our editor-curated picks to gift your friends and family some seriously cool tech while saving yourself some serious cash. Looking for the best of the best, regardless of price? Check the top products we've tested overall, as well as the latest winners of PCMag's Editors' Choice award. Apple’s $599 MacBook Neo lands as not only the top budget MacBook, but the best low-cost laptop, hands-down. The Neo runs on an A18 Pro iPhone processor with 8GB of memory and a 256GB solid-state drive, to amazing effect for the casual tasks it's intended for. We even stretched it beyond that, especially in games, and found that the Neo makes an honest attempt, which is more than we can say about most budget Windows laptops. Apple rounds out the package with a rigid, premium MacBook Air-like chassis, a perky Liquid Retina display, and long battery life. Minimizing concessions and maximizing upside are key when choosing a cheap laptop, and the Lenovo Chromebook Duet Gen 9 successfully threads that needle. This low-cost detachable is ideal for students, younger users, and budget-conscious buyers thanks to its sharp screen and quality build. The performance will hardly wow you, but it’s capable for its intended purposes. This is a well-made and versatile entry point into the ChromeOS and Android app ecosystem for work and education. Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 (2025) We love Asus’ latest version of the Chromebook Plus CX34 because it delivers impressive performance and essential features at an unbeatable price. From the powerful processor and solid design to the AI features and great port selection, this machine handles everyday tasks with ease. It’s a great choice for students or anyone else who’s looking for a powerful, affordable Chromebook. This standout model also earned our Editors' Choice award, reinforcing its position as the top pick in the budget Chromebook category. The Katana 15 HX is the best-performing budget gaming laptop we’ve tested, thanks in part to its GeForce RTX 5050 GPU. Nvidia’s DLSS 4 technology empowers this system to play the latest DLSS-compliant titles smoothly with high visual settings. Some of this is achieved through “artificial” frames, but that’s a small concession to make in the budget tier. The laptop is sturdily built with a comfortable keyboard, is quick enough for general productivity, and has reasonably long battery life. We’d like to see roomier storage capacity, but considering the price, this is the current best entry-level gaming-laptop deal. The TCL Flip 4 is a clamshell feature phone that connects to the latest generation cellular networks, 5G. This light and sturdy phone features a full physical keypad, a 5MP camera for quick snaps, and a new hinge that makes it easier to open than the previous edition. Perhaps best of all, the Flip 4 offers excellent call quality, thanks to its loud speakers and high-quality microphones. Beyond that, it also features some basic apps, such as a web browser and YouTube, if you want to do more than just talk. For just under $200, the Samsung Galaxy A17 5G offers nearly all you need from a low-cost phone. Highlights include a large display with a quick 90Hz refresh rate, top-notch battery life, respectable 5G speeds, and a capable camera suite. Samsung promises six years of OS and security updates, meaning you can feel safe in using the phone for years. A fingerprint reader for biometric security and a microSD card slot for memory cards put the cap on this budget-friendly phone. The iPhone 17e is the most affordable iPhone you can get. It’s got Face ID, a perky screen, and a quick A18 processor. It also has a second-generation, Apple-designed modem and excellent battery life. Add in the full capabilities of Apple Intelligence, a solid camera, and fast wireless performance, and you have a fine way to enter the iPhone ecosystem for $200 less than the next-best option. Amazon Fire HD 8 (2024) This simple 8-inch slate isn't a powerhouse, by any means, but it offers easy access to gobs of media at a price that most competing 8-inch tablets can't match. A clear step up from Amazon's extremely entry-level Fire 7, it's an appealing option for Amazon Prime subscribers, first-time tablet buyers, or anyone seeking a robust spare slate to carry on adventures. Apple iPad (11th Gen, 2025) Apple's 11-inch iPad, starting at $349, is all the tablet that most people need. Its A16 processor is powerful enough to run Apple Intelligence, and its landscape-mounted, wide-angle front camera is perfect for FaceTime and Zoom calls. It also works with the Apple Pencil (USB-C), supports Wi-Fi 6, and has a USB-C port. It’s the best iPad for most people and our Editors’ Choice winner. Shoppers seeking a cheap traditional desktop usually just want the basics without breaking the bank, and this Acer tower delivers. At $599.99, our review model has a snappy-enough 14th Gen Intel processor, 8GB of memory, and a 512GB SSD. It also offers Wi-Fi 6E and other extras like dual HDMI monitor support and an SD card reader. A good value with acceptable caveats, this Aspire system can slot right into your living room or home office. Dell 24 All-in-One (EC24250) Dell’s mainstream 24-inch AIO presents an attractive design, wireless peripherals, and ample connectivity for everyday computing. We'd like a peppier processor and better audio, but it's a decent deal when on sale. It hits the mark in several areas, including visual quality, port selection, webcam fidelity, and bundled wireless peripherals. This desktop is easily capable of day-to-day tasks and streaming. Dell's sub-$1,000 configurations of this AIO PC are a decent value, and the version we tested has dropped to as low as $799.99. Intel launched the Ultra 5 250K Plus at an aggressively competitive $199. It offers general-purpose processing power rivaling far more expensive processors, and it also delivers improved gaming performance thanks to design changes from the original Arrow Lake. The integrated graphics built into this processor are also quite capable and can be used for light gaming, so long as you stick to older titles or reduce the graphics settings. All together, the Ultra 5 250K Plus is exactly what we hope to see in a budget processor. Looking for an ATX case packed with features and a distinctive design for under $100? Funky translucent front-panel trim, a trio of colorful ARGB fans, and an angled interior design set this classic midtower chassis apart from the budget pack. (It even supports reverse-connector motherboards for a visually clean build on the cheap.) We had a few quibbles, but this ultimately gives off the vibe of a pricier case than its MSRP suggests. Available at this writing at a sizable $200 discount off its $499.99 list price, the ASRock Z890 Taichi brings a true flagship motherboard to as close to the budget zone as possible. It’s rare to find a $300 motherboard with advanced features like these, such as a substantial power management design that exceeds what most boards at this price provide. ASRock bolsters that with PCI Express 5.0 support, six M.2 expansion slots, a top-tier PC audio system, and class-leading networking hardware. It’s a strong pick for a top-end Intel motherboard at a very attractive price…so long as the sale lasts. Sandisk's WD Blue SN5100 delivers strong performance, achieving one of the best scores for a PCIe 4.0 drive on the PCMark 10 Overall Storage test. The SN5100 comes with a free download of Acronis backup and migration software, as well as the Sandisk Dashboard utility. It's also designed for energy efficiency (note that it ships without a heatsink or heat spreader). As a DRAM-less internal SSD with QLC NAND and a PCI Express 4.0 drive, it was once an excellent budget option, starting at just $58 when it launched. But due to the RAM shortage, it now starts at $120. You might be able to find it slightly cheaper, since WD is rebranding the Blue family of drives. Intel’s “Battlemage” graphics architecture is an evolutionary step forward, with greatly improved performance and efficiency compared with previous versions. Arguably the best aspect of the Arc B580 graphics card is its low price, though, which undercuts its closest AMD and Nvidia competitors. Add in measurably better performance than these competitors, particularly at higher resolutions, and you get a graphics card that’s inexpensive yet still lets you enjoy playing the latest games. Although a relatively large screen for a pittance is the Philips 271V8LB’s chief selling point, this 27-inch display—which you can be yours for barely a C-note—also offers the superior contrast of a VA panel, full sRGB color coverage, a 100Hz refresh rate, and adaptive sync. Otherwise, the 271V8LB’s budget-monitor DNA shows in its minimal port selection, limited ergonomics, multiple tiny control buttons, and modest resolution (1080p) for its screen size. A memory shortage that could last for years means that even relatively low-priced SSDs are no longer the great bargains we saw a year ago. One external SSD that stands out for quality while remaining somewhat reasonably priced is the Crucial X10, launched in mid-2025. The X10 set new high scores for write speed among the Gen 2x2 SSDs we have tested in both the CrystalDiskMark and Blackmagic tests, and did well in our other benchmarks. Available in five capacities up to 8TB, it makes a good scratch disk for creatives, or a home for game, photo, or media libraries. It was a good value when it launched, starting at $120, and with the 4TB version we tested going for $330. The 4TB is now $425, though you may be able to find it at a discount as inventory peters out due to Micron's decision to kill the Crucial brand. Epson EcoTank ET-1910 Wireless Color Supertank Printer In a world of inkjets dominated by all-in-one designs, Epson's standout EcoTank ET-1910 jettisons the scan and copy functions. That makes for a tank-based printer that's uncommonly affordable to both buy and run. Unlike most inkjet-printer competitors, it doesn't force you to choose between a low initial price and low running costs. Its $159.99 list price includes enough ink for thousands of pages, and it has a low cost per page after that. It's slower than some cartridge-based competition, but for most use at home, in a dorm, or the like, the savings are well worth a little extra printing time, and enough to make the ET-1910 our top pick for a low-cost inkjet printer. If you don't need a network connection, print infrequently, and never require color output, the HP LaserJet M209d is well worth its reasonable price. Its print text quality is top-notch compared with both mono lasers in its price range and in the broader segment. The lack of Ethernet and Wi-Fi support are downsides, but the printer's low cost and solid performance make it very suitable for single users with light needs. The Bambu Lab A1 mini is a top-notch 3D printer for beginners or hobbyists seeking an affordable option. It's easy to get going, fast, and even capable of four-color printing. Most importantly, it makes great-looking prints. Priced at $249 but offered with an add-on module (bringing the price to $399) that can print with any or all of four different-colored filaments, the A1 mini makes multicolor creations easy. It’s the lowest-cost four-color fused deposition modeling (FDM) printer currently on the market. And with ease of use that rivals pricier models from other vendors, it’s a nearly perfect device for someone new to 3D printing. Elegoo has long been a driver in making resin printing more affordable, but the Mars 5 Ultra is next-level, even on that score. An ideal resin model for first-timers, it delivers a host of conveniences for this notoriously messy and hard-to-master means of printing: a tilting resin vat (designed to reduce peel forces and improve your chances of a successful print), automatic build-plate leveling, and an onboard camera for monitoring and time-lapse recording print progress. Simply put, it simplifies your early prints and reduces common failure points, all at a great price. If you seek a smartphone-companion photo printer but don't want to be stuck with just rectangular business-card size or square Instagram-style prints, check out the Canon Selphy QX20. Unlike most competing models, which offer just one of the above formats, the QX20 can handle either. It also produces high-quality, long-lasting prints thanks to its dye-sub technology. The Epson Perfection V39 II is an excellent budget flatbed photo scanner with robust software that makes it especially suitable for creative types and hobbyists. A high-resolution 4,800dpi scan engine, top-notch OCR accuracy, and streamlined task processes help it outclass the competition. The N6 Pro, which is widely available for less than its list price, claims a staggering 700 ANSI lumens of brightness, and it's unquestionably the brightest projector we've seen in the sub-$200 range. You don't have to spin up a new email address, and the service integrates automatically with Apple Mail, Gmail, and Outlook. Forgot your all-important encryption password? A unique and sophisticated key-recovery system lets you get it back with a little help from your friends. Proton Pass looks great, works smoothly, and is open-source, meaning the code is under constant review. The robust free plan includes password health monitoring, along with storage and syncing for unlimited passwords across all of your devices. You can also create up to 10 email aliases, so say goodbye to spam forever. Proton Pass has browser extensions for Brave, Chrome, Edge, and Firefox, a web-based vault, and apps for Android, ChromeOS, iOS, Linux, macOS, and Windows. It's hard to beat free, and if you're looking to start a podcast or record music, or just need a tool to assemble and convert some audio samples, Audacity is your program. Now owned by Muse Group, this venerable software started life as an open-source, two-channel stereo editor, but it has grown and expanded to include multitrack recording, many effects, and spectral and spectrogram views for sample-level editing. Despite unlimited undos and redos and a new clip editor, Audacity is destructive at heart, with no support for VSTs or other real-time plug-ins. But if you're careful with your edits, Audacity will get you where you need to go with no money down—or ever, in fact. If you need a place to store your photos online for free, use Google Photos. It's a complete consumer photo workflow app for mobile and web that lets you automatically back up, organize, edit, and share your images. It no longer gives you unlimited storage (free users get a respectable 15GB), but its capabilities remain impressive. And if you want more storage, a $1.99-per-month Google One subscription includes 100GB. If you intend to learn a language for free, Duolingo is your best option. It might not make you proficient, but it supplements live classes well and can help you get the basics down. Duolingo impressively presents learning material for more than 30 languages in a clear structure and places you at the appropriate difficulty level, given your existing knowledge. The interface is top-notch, and we enjoy the engaging podcasts that accompany more traditional exercises. If you want an ad-free experience and personalized instruction, consider paying for a Super Duolingo subscription. If you want to dip your toes into the world of AI chatbots, Gemini offers not only excellent response quality but an impressive range of free luxuries, such as access to its most advanced models, cloud storage, deep research, and video generation. You can also use Gemini's top-notch Nano Banana image editing and generation model, which won our Technical Excellence award, entirely for free. Considering that to-do list apps are a dime a dozen, it's downright shocking that so few of them are truly helpful, well designed, and affordable. Todoist, however, is all that. Whether you use the wonderful free version or pay to upgrade to an inexpensive Premium account, Todoist is clearly the best to-do list app on the market. It works on all your devices, tracks your productivity, and lets you geek out on organizing and analyzing your life. If you need an app to organize your tasks, either by yourself or in collaboration with others, you need Todoist. Tired of shopping using cash or cards? Apple Pay lets you purchase nearly anything by holding your iPhone over an NFC terminal at a store. It has other cool functionalities, too, including peer-to-peer money transfers and the ability to house commuter passes, digital tickets, and ID cards. Don't have an iPhone? The excellent Google Wallet provides many similar features on Android phones. A dating app like Tinder, which prioritizes fast hook-ups over drawn-out relationship analysis, needs to have as many users as possible. That's why it costs you nothing to sign up and instantly start swiping to let people know whether you find them hot or not. If you want to pay money for perks such as profile boosts and Super Likes, you can do that, too. Still, free Tinder promises plenty of potential romantic rewards, unlike eHarmony's no-cost tier. Wix is an excellent website builder—and unlike many of its competitors such as Gator or Squarespace, you can use it for free. You won't get a custom domain, and you'll need to be okay with ads appearing on your site, but in return you'll enjoy powerful tools for building fantastic desktop and mobile sites. Besides, there's nothing stopping you from upgrading later on. An extension of Google’s entertainment arm and an offshoot of the enormous YouTube platform, YouTube Music lets you enjoy its many ad-supported offerings without spending a dime (though you can upgrade to a premium account to ditch the ads). YouTube Music's community uploads, music videos, podcasts, scrolling lyrics, and recently added Samples (a music discovery tool) all make for an excellent package. It lacks hi-res audio, but YouTube Music is hard to beat for recommendation-based listening. Tubi doesn’t offer a limited free tier that simply acts as a teaser for a premium video streaming plan. Instead, it serves up its entire library of major studio releases—for free! Sure, it has ads, and certain movies and TV shows may come and go without warning. Still, Tubi proves you can enjoy great streaming video content without paying for a subscription. Zoom has remained relevant by pivoting from a simple video conferencing app to a more comprehensive business communication tool. Now known as Zoom Workplace, the service features an AI assistant and new collaboration tools that you can use outside of meetings. Its robust free tier still offers 40-minute meetings, basic whiteboard features, team chat, and a 100-person attendee capacity, too.

Centuries before skiers started carving down its slopes, Val d’Isère was a remote mountain farming community – and its 1664 church steeple still stands at the heart of what was the village. Its transition into a world-class retreat started slowly, beginning with its very first hotel in 1888 after a new mountain road opened up access and accelerating when the pioneering Téléphérique de Solaise cable car was completed in 1942. Today, however, is another matter entirely. This shimmering enclave is now home to some of the French Alps’ most wondrous private chalets, and a glut of stylish snow-seekers make their annual pilgrimage every season without fail. In turn, the private homestay scene nowadays melds the area’s traditional Savoyard stone and timber architecture with state-of-the-art design and amenities ripe for the modern traveller. So, whether your priority is quick and easy access to the slope for early morning kickoffs, or simply a cosy fireside lounge to curl up on a long lazy afternoon, there’s a smart address for you.
